reading.body:
The AI Policy Network Inc. appears in 5 AI lobbying filings, naming 13 lobbyists and 16 bills, all from 2025 or later.

The structure is a single client with a deep bench. Five lobbyists appear on all 5 filings, and eight more appear on 1 to 3, which is the pattern of a firm staffing one account broadly rather than spreading across many clients. The 16 named bills are the substance of the work: this is one organization tracking a wide slate of AI legislation, not a coalition of companies.

For AI specifically, this is the policy layer that sits upstream of compute. Bills that shape data center siting, energy contracts, or model regulation determine what can be built and powered. The filing record shows which legislative vehicles are in play, but not which direction the client argued on any of them.

What the data does not cover: the content of the filings, the positions taken, spending amounts, or outcomes. A filing reports that a client lobbied on an issue, not what it wanted. The bill numbers are listed without subject matter, so the reader cannot tell from this data alone whether they concern AI directly or adjacent topics.
